Mix of short-answer (2–4 marks), description (6 marks) and extended evaluation/discussion questions (12 marks, split AO1/AO3). No choice within sections. No calculator required.",

  },
  "title": "AQA A-level Psychology Paper 1: Introductory topics in psychology — Original Practice Paper",
  "instructions": [
    "Answer all questions in all four sections.",
    "There are 96 marks in total. Time allowed: 2 hours.",
    "Use black ink. Write answers in the spaces provided in a real sitting.",
    "Questions requiring application should be answered with reference to the scenario or material provided.",
    "Extended questions (12 marks) are marked for knowledge (AO1) and evaluation/analysis (AO3); quality of written communication is assessed in extended answers."
  ],
  "companionDocuments": [],

  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "label": "Question 1",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by internalisation in social influence.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "label": "Question 2",
      "prompt": "Priya is new to her sixth form. She wears the same style of clothes as her friends because she wants to be liked by them, but privately she still prefers her old style. In her psychology class, she accepts her teacher's explanation of a study because she believes the teacher knows more about the subject than she does.\n\nIdentify the type of conformity shown by Priya in each situation. Explain one reason why each type occurred.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q3",
      "label": "Question 3",
      "prompt": "Outline two variations in Asch's original conformity study and describe the effect each variation had on conformity rates.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q4",
      "label": "Question 4",
      "prompt": "Discuss obedience to authority. In your answer, you should refer to Milgram's baseline study and evaluate explanations of obedience.",
      "marks": 12,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q5",
      "label": "Question 5",
      "prompt": "Define the term 'proactive interference'.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q6",
      "label": "Question 6",
      "prompt": "Tomas learned to play the piano using one fingering system. He has now started learning a second piece that requires a different fingering for the same notes, and he keeps making errors on the new piece. When he plays the old piece, however, he plays it perfectly.\n\nUse your knowledge of interference theory to explain Tomas's errors on the new piece.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q7",
      "label": "Question 7",
      "prompt": "Describe the working memory model. In your answer you should refer to the central executive, the phonological loop and the visuo-spatial sketchpad.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q8",
      "label": "Question 8",
      "prompt": "Discuss factors affecting the accuracy of eyewitness testimony. In your answer you should refer to misleading information and evaluate research in this area.",
      "marks": 12,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q9",
      "label": "Question 9",
      "prompt": "What is meant by the term 'reciprocity' in caregiver–infant interactions?",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q10",
      "label": "Question 10",
      "prompt": "A researcher observes a 12-month-old child with a stranger and then with the child's mother. The child shows moderate separation anxiety when the mother leaves, seeks contact with her when she returns, and is wary of the stranger even when the mother is present.\n\nIdentify the attachment type the researcher is likely to classify this child as. Explain two behaviours from the observation that support your classification.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q11",
      "label": "Question 11",
      "prompt": "Describe the effects of institutionalisation on children, using research on Romanian orphanages to support your answer.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q12",
      "label": "Question 12",
      "prompt": "Discuss Bowlby's theory of maternal deprivation. In your answer you should describe the theory and evaluate the research evidence supporting and challenging it.",
      "marks": 12,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q13",
      "label": "Question 13",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by 'introspection' in Wundt's work.",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q14",
      "label": "Question 14",
      "prompt": "A teacher praises students with a sticker each time they complete homework. One student, who previously never did homework, now completes it regularly. Another student, who was praised for shouting out answers, now shouts out more often.\n\nUse concepts from operant conditioning to explain the change in each student's behaviour.",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q15",
      "label": "Question 15",
      "prompt": "Describe the role of the unconscious and the structure of personality (id, ego and superego) in the psychodynamic approach.",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q16",
      "label": "Question 16",
      "prompt": "Discuss the cognitive approach in psychology. In your answer you should describe key assumptions and features of the approach, including schemas and theoretical models, and evaluate the approach using comparison with other approaches.",
      "marks": 12,
      "assets": []
    }
  ],

  "examinerInsights": [
    "In 12-mark discussion questions, candidates often write long description but thin evaluation; plan roughly balanced AO1 and AO3 content.",
    "Application questions require explicit use of scenario details — naming the concept alone earns little credit.",
    "For research-based questions, evaluation should include methodological points (sample, validity, ethics) rather than generic statements.",
    "Timing: roughly 1.25 minutes per mark; the four 12-mark questions deserve about 15 minutes each including planning.",
    "In the Approaches section, comparison with other approaches is frequently omitted and costs marks."
